root.name: Philidor Defense: Morphy Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4

overview: After the d-pawn trade White does not recapture at once but develops the bishop, aiming for a Scotch Gambit-like game. Black can hold the d4 pawn with ...c5 or ...Nc6, or return it, and White gets a lead in development with an open centre. I am unsure of the exact main line, so I judge it as a quick-development gambit that Black can usually neutralise.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Bc4, O-O and Re1 or Ng5, regaining the pawn with Nxd4 when useful.
Use the lead in development and open lines to attack f7.

black_ideas.idea: Hold d4 with ...c5 or return the pawn, then complete development with ...Nf6 and ...Be7.
Neutralise the bishop with ...Be6 and trade pieces.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after d-pawn trades, pieces active.

character.notes: Open lines and tempo play, but Black can simplify; known as tactical rather than solid.

gambit.notes: White does not recapture immediately; Black can hold the pawn with ...c5, though White often regains it by force.

soundness.notes: Not refuted; Black has several comfortable options.

structure.notes: Central pawns come off and lines open.

approach.notes: Rarely chosen by strong players; a surprise try.

level.notes: Little theory; plans are simple but unusual.

character.reason: Open play and quick development, though Black can simplify.

gambit.reason: A pawn is nominally offered but Black can hold it only with care and White often regains it.

structure.reason: Central pawns exchanged and open lines.

plans.reason: White aims pieces at f7 and develops fast.
